key_insight: PoliVEM unifies multiple solid-mechanics virtual element formulations in a single Python-driven C++ framework by reusing common mesh, DOF, projection, assembly, and solver infrastructure.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, extensible foundation for polygonal and polyhedral analysis of beams, elasticity, diffusion, and hyperelasticity with consistent element-level treatment.
method: Common C++17 core with Python interface for modular VEM solvers
Shared hierarchy for vertex/edge/face/cell DOFs plus cached projection operators
Supports static condensation, coloured sparse assembly, Newton solving, and time integration
evidence_signal: The paper validates the framework with polynomial reproduction, recovery after static condensation, higher-order DOF handling, patch tests, stiffness spectra, and comparisons to independent finite element results.
watch_item: High-order polynomial bases can scale poorly on anisotropic cells, and sparse direct factorization memory can become a limiting cost.
paper_title: PoliVEM: a Python-driven virtual element framework for computational solid mechanics
